entries.migrationNote: GUI sends terminal-equivalent /capabilities text only; TUI-native discovery owns ranking and expansion.
Presentation packages expose renderer/viewer/workbench capability only; GUI may render, focus, and collect input, but does not register TUI task skills or execute providers.
Policy, budget, confidence, repair, and completion gates remain TUI-native decisions; GUI may display state or collect confirmation only.
Provider routing must fail closed when the selected route is unavailable; no silent OpenAI fallback is allowed.
Verifier owns verdict, confidence, critique, and repair hints; GUI only renders explicit verifier output.
Workspace proposals are staging artifacts; final promotion target is Codex native.

External app connectors talk only to the TUI Host. They may ingest external messages as Agent Host input envelopes; admitted messages must be appended to the Agent Host thread ledger so Web chat can render first-class external user messages. Resource/action flows return refs, drafts, approval requests, and audit refs; GUI sends text, renders refs, and collects confirmation when it participates.

entries.migrationNote: Browser runtime shared schema/helper code lives in runtime-contract; observe/web owns TUI provider-facing wrapper; BrowserHostSession is the only live browser owner for external HTTP/HTTPS navigation, click/double-click/mouse-down/mouse-move/mouse-up/drag/type/press/scroll/cursor-hit-test action input, native-or-streaming live surface, frame/state transports, screenshot/DOM/AX/console/network refs, takeover refs, and browser_search search-result refs. Desktop final live path is an Electron WebContentsView native embedded surface adapter reached through SCIFORGE_BROWSER_HOST_NATIVE_ADAPTER_URL by the workspace-server BrowserHostSession driver; the desktop shell only attaches bounds and forwards the same session surface, so it is not a second truth source. Workspace Writer exposes browser-host-session/browser-host-search in /health and owns /api/sciforge/browser-host/* routes, including /computer-use-actions for user and agent mouse/keyboard intent. Web shell frame-stream is a non-desktop owner stream/diagnostic/evidence transport, not a native desktop replacement; the /frame route is evidence/manual inspection only and must not become the Browser pane live view replacement. GUI may preflight health, start runtime services, switch to the effective writer URL, attach native surface bounds, and render host-returned cursor/caret/pointer projection, but remains a shell/adapter; preflight must reject stale Workspace Writers whose /health endpoints omit computer-use-actions or frame-stream instead of treating state-only refs as a live browser. Tauri, Electron, and Web are shell/adapter layers only. browser-workbench owns right-pane presentation. GUI sends /browser text, renders refs-first projections, and displays the one host-owned live surface. Same-origin proxy, static snapshots, PDFs, documents, old frames, Electron <webview>, system popups, and replay artifacts are evidence/artifacts or explicit handoff only and must not become a second interactive browser truth or replacement interaction path.
Browser, terminal, and workspace file surfaces are package-owned presentation modules. src/ui may connect host helpers and view-local events, but package renderers must remain presentation-only.

forbiddenOwners: third-party virtual screen UI as product truth
entries.migrationNote: VirtualAppScreen final C is a package-owned Native Host/control plane. The current package boundary includes README, capability manifest, public API/session/error/ledger contracts, fail-closed/in-memory contract smoke, grant validation, host-owned ledger validators, viewer/runtime grant validation, and dogfood Native Host passed gates for nativeHost, humanInputHotPath, automationBarrierRefs, and backgroundEvidenceRefs. This proves contract/gate alignment only, not real platform provider completion or user-level pass. The host owns permission preflight, virtual display/app surface lifecycle, target app attach, surface presentation, human fire-and-release input, automation barriers, live attach grants, and host-owned evidence writing. Platform providers and third-party virtual screen tools are adapters, references, benchmarks, or diagnostics only; they cannot bypass host grants, execute product input directly, or mint user-level acceptance.
